case_name: Mehboob Batcha & Ors v State Rep. By Supdt. Of Police
respondent:
State Rep. By Supdt. Of Police
Supreme Court of India

29 March 2011
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1511 OF 2003
The Judgment was delivered by : Markandey Katju, J.
"Bane hain ahal-e-hawas muddai bhi munsif bhi Kise vakeel karein kisse munsifi chaahen"
Faiz Ahmed Faiz :
1.  If ever there was a case which cried out for death penalty it is this one, but it is deeply regrettable that not only was no such penalty imposed but not even a charge under Section 302 IPC was framed against the accused by the Courts below.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.  The facts in detail have been stated in the impugned judgment of the High Court as well as of the trial court and hence we are not repeating the same here, except where necessary.
3.  The appellants are policemen who wrongfully confined one Nandagopal in police custody in Police Station Annamalai Nagar on suspicion of theft from 30.5.1992 till 2.6.1992 and beat him to death there with lathis, and also gang raped his wife Pad
facts: The appellants are policemen who wrongfully confined one Nandagopal in police custody in Police Station Annamalai Nagar on suspicion of theft from 30.5.1992 till 2.6.1992 and beat him to death there with lathis, and also gang raped his wife Padmini in a barbaric manner.
The accused also confined several other persons (who were witnesses) and beat them in the police station with lathis.
Padmini has given her evidence in great detail and we see no reason to disbelieve the same.
petitioner_arguments: To prove the charges the prosecution examined as many as 37 witnesses, and they have proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
court_reasoning: We have read her evidence which discloses the inhuman and savage manner in which the accused, who were police personnel, treated Nandagopal and Padmini.

holding: Both the trial Court and the High Court have found the appellants guilty and we see no reason to disagree with their verdict.
